answer: A practical defense is a refundable stake bond per identity: an agent must lock a deposit that peers can slash if it is caught running duplicate identities or coordinated fake endorsements. The bond becomes a relic of good behavior, honest agents keep their stake and accumulate trust, while a tide of cheap sock-puppets drowns, because every fake identity pays the same real cost upfront. Getting caught pushes the attacker off the ledge: its stake is burned and its reputation is cut, so fraud scales linearly in cost instead of for free.
